paragraphs.source_en: After they had gone about ten chō, events unfolded just as Sannojō had said: more than two hundred Iga warriors, using their familiarity with the local terrain, guarded Ieyasu and his party from the front, rear, left, and right. Only when he saw this did Ieyasu breathe a heartfelt sigh of relief. He was moved and rueful, yet at the same time reassured.

paragraphs.source_en: A country, too, has an unseen pillar holding it aloft... Once that pillar falls, the whole realm is instantly plunged into chaos. As the turmoil deepens, people begin, almost without realizing it, to yearn for another pillar to uphold the realm.

paragraphs.source_en: The way beneath their feet was still a mountain path, now vanishing, now reappearing. As he walked, Ieyasu distinguished between trails trodden by people and those made by animals. Suddenly, he felt like summoning the bloodied farmer for a talk.

paragraphs.source_en: Nobunaga's unexpected death had brought him to his second great peril since the Battle of Mikatagahara. paragraphs.source_en: In truth, Ieyasu had not felt heartfelt pity or concern for the farmers.
